CTC, OLTCs, and bushings do not have unique HTS codes and are instead tracked under broader product categories. Even where codes appear closely aligned (e.g., bushings under 8546), these items could be used across electrical industries beyond transformers. Accordingly, import data should be interpreted as a proxy for supply chain reliance rather than a precise measure of product-specific imports. b For components such as insulating paper/pressboard, transformer oils and additives, CTC conductors, OLTCs, and bushings, publicly available HTS categories are too broad to isolate transformer-specific products. While reports suggest limited U.S. manufacturing capacity for these items, no public data are available to quantify exact import reliance. c https://pubs.usgs.gov/periodicals/mcs2025/mcs2025-copper.pdf d For transformer kraft paper-based insulation materials, we assume the most relevant tariff classifications are HTS 4804.31.2000 (uncoated kraft condenser paper, unbleached, 30–150 g/m²), HTS 4804.39.2000 (condenser paper, bleached, ≤150 g/m²). These codes align with the kraft insulating papers widely used in LPTs for windings, spacers, and barriers, whereas other codes under Chapter 48 generally apply to packaging or printing grades not relevant to electrical applications. e For transformer paperboard-based insulation materials, we assume the most relevant tariff classification is HTS 4805.93.2000 (electrical pressboard, uncoated, ≥225 g/m²). This code aligns with the pressboard widely used in LPTs for windings, spacers, and barriers, whereas other codes under Chapter 48 generally apply to packaging or printing grades not relevant to electrical applications. The stacked bar charts in Figures 5–7 show the U.S. import customs value of GOES, refined copper, and LPTs as finished products by country of origin from 2015 to 2024. U.S. imports of GOES have been volatile over the past decade. Japan and South Korea consistently dominate as the largest suppliers to the United States, while Canada, Mexico, Brazil, and several European countries supply smaller volumes. 13 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies at www.nlr.gov/publications.
